title: Longest Word
description:
Write the whole program. Read the input however you like.

The input is one line of words separated by single spaces. Print the longest word.

If several words tie for the longest, print the one that appears first.

Example input:
```
the quick brown fox
```
Expected output: `quick` (both "quick" and "brown" have 5 letters, and "quick" comes first).
hints: Concept: `line.split(" ")` turns a sentence into an array of words. Once you have an array, finding the longest is like finding the largest number.

Approach: remember the best word so far. Go through the words, and replace the best word only when the current one is strictly longer. Using "strictly longer" (not "longer or equal") keeps the first word when there's a tie.

Pseudocode:
  line = read one line
  words = split line by spaces
  best = words[0]
  for each word in words:
      if word.length > best.length:
          best = word
  print best

workedExample.title: Shortest Word Length
workedExample.description: Read a line of words and print the length of the shortest word.
workedExample.explanation:
This version reads the line with `BufferedReader`; `Scanner.nextLine()` would work just as well.

Splitting turns the problem into an array problem. Then it's the familiar "remember the best so far" loop. For your problem, remember the word itself instead of just its length.

walkthrough.note: "quick" has 5 letters, more than 3. best becomes "quick".
"brown" also has 5 letters. It isn't strictly longer, so best stays "quick".
"fox" has 3 letters. best stays "quick". Print quick.

mistakes.hint: "quick" and "brown" are both 5 letters. When there's a tie, keep the first word: replace it only when a word is strictly longer (`>`, not `>=`).
